videos.script: One Redis on one machine dies with the machine. {{one}} So you add replicas. Each one receives every write the primary makes, a moment after the primary has answered. {{replicas}} Then something has to notice the primary is gone and promote a replica. That is Sentinel: three small processes that vote. {{sentinel}} You will stop the primary and read the failover in their logs, line by line. {{failover}} Then the promise from lesson 1. You cut the primary off the network and write to it. It answers OK. {{partition}} The Sentinels promote a replica on the other side. When the network heals, your order is gone, and nothing ever reported an error. {{lost}} WAIT tells you a write is at risk. A minimum of replicas makes the primary refuse. Neither closes the window completely. {{wait}} Last, Redis Cluster: six nodes, sixteen thousand slots, redirections, and a primary that dies and is replaced from inside. {{cluster}} And the question that picks between the two. {{which}}
